sentences.text: The NSW Independent Commission Against Corruption examines how public sector managers can improve procurement systems and influence staff behaviour to reduce corruption.
sentences.support: The major purpose of this report, therefore, is to illustrate the variety of tools available to managers

sentences.text: It considers procurement structures, purchasing processes and staff management, using investigation case studies to illustrate control weaknesses.
sentences.support: Throughout the report, case studies of real investigations are used to illustrate weaknesses related to structures, processes and people

sentences.text: The Commission concludes that relying on policies, codes and training controls only a small share of corruption risks.
sentences.support: Simple reliance on policies, codes, and training will control only a small proportion of corruption.

sentences.text: The Commission advises managers to combine approaches suited to their agency’s risks, rather than prescribing formal recommendations.
sentences.support: The advice in this report is not presented as a list of formal recommendations.

findings.quote: When it comes to procurement, there is no single method of corruption control.
Simple reliance on policies, codes, and training will control only a small proportion of corruption.

notes: No separate summary. The report expressly states that it does not present formal recommendations; its conclusion is on PDF page 35.
